hypothesis: Fusing decode hyper Q8 up projection, sigmoid and four-stream mix can reduce complete-block latency through fewer dispatches and intermediates.
expected_effect: Exact outputs with a whole-cycle wall improvement whose paired upper95 ratio is below1 and frequency-weighted median saving reaches20ms/token.
controlled_change: Standalone appended Metal kernel only; four actual raw inputs from GDN layer0 and attention layer3, real original mixed weights, unchanged norm/down/activation and BF16 injection. Five alternating complete-cycle pairs; production native build unchanged.
correctness: 364 Python tests pass and ten focused tests rechecked after final preparation. Four complete reference outputs and injections match native capture byte-for-byte, fused outputs match reference, twelve supplemental synthetic edge cases match, and input hashes/neighbor guards remain intact. Separate Metal API/shader validation passed.
outcome: Completed in3.106seconds. Primary whole-cycle geometric wall ratio1.01101376 (95%1.00457326–1.01749555); all five cycles slower. Median frequency projection−0.315703ms/token; clean memory,28.43MiB shared buffers,63.77MiB physical peak. Lower encoding cost was outweighed by higher GPU time.
smallest_experiment: Do not integrate or long-qualify this fusion. Select a different intervention from the completed request dependency budget; preserve this composition as tested negative evidence.
limitations: Four captured blocks, not all96 blocks or full-model state; fixture native producer identity is retained.
Repeated resident weights and preallocated scratch differ from live requests, SSD streaming and native buffer lifetimes.
Frequency projection is a screening heuristic, not predicted request savings. Five pairs in one process may be correlated.
Memory counters are sampled at boundaries plus process lifetime peaks; device swap includes other processes.
No footprint saving is inferred from eliminated logical intermediates; both probe arms coexist.
